ADAPTED FEARS for this legal topic, as instructed by the orchestrator: the couple persona's fear 2 (planning from the other side of the world) becomes 'we have to get legal paperwork right in Greece from Sydney, across time zones, with town halls that open on weekdays and may need us in person', and fear 4 (budget across currencies and contracts in Italian) becomes 'paperwork, fees and translations in Greek and in euros, in an alphabet we cannot read'. payload.search_intent: Informational with commercial follow-through. The reader has chosen or shortlisted Greece and wants to know how the legal marriage works for Australians: what the licence is, how long it takes, which documents come from which Australian office, and whether the marriage counts at home. Many arrive having read 'eight days' and want to know if that dictates their travel dates.
payload.angle: The real rule, made usable from Australia. Official Greek sources say the licence wait is one week from a complete file, not eight days; the piece shows what starts the clock, what restarts it, and why couples who live in Australia may not go through the Greek licence at all in some municipalities (they bring a CNI from DFAT instead). Then it turns the paperwork into a calendar counted back from the wedding date and a wedding-week timetable that fits town-hall visits around guests arriving. Every legal line cites a Greek or Australian government page, and every rule ends with 'confirm with your municipality and for your own passports'.
serp_gaps_to_win: Correct the 'eight days' figure with official sources (gov.gr registry, Municipality of Athens) and explain where the number likely comes from. No ranking page does this; two misquote gov.gr.

Resident vs visiting couple: the official pages treat them differently (gov.gr and Athens describe a licence for residents; Chania and Heraklion describe a home-country licence for foreigners living abroad). No ranking page explains this.

Australia does not issue a 'marriage licence': explain the DFAT CNI as what Greek town halls receive, including that the acceptable place of issue (DFAT in Australia vs Embassy Athens) can differ by municipality or church (Australian Embassy Athens).

Translation rules, sourced and current: resolve the conflict between the Embassy page (MFA translation section only) and the Ministry of Interior's 2021 circulars on a new official translation system. Nobody has this right.

Wedding-week timetable: weekday office hours, in-person submission, witnesses, interpreter, registration after a weekend wedding, all fitted around guest arrivals. Shown as an example, never a promise.
Recognition in Australia from an Australian official source (Attorney-General's Department or Smartraveller), answering the paying parent directly. Ranking pages answer this only for the US.
PAA 'How long can an Australian citizen stay in Greece?': one sourced line (Schengen short-stay rule and any ETIAS status, from Smartraveller).

outline.h2: What a Greek marriage licence is, and whether you need one
outline.answers: What the licence (adeia gamou) is, who issues it, and whether an Australian couple living in Australia goes through it.
must_include: The licence is issued by the municipality (the mayor) under the Civil Code; fee EUR 18, valid six months (gov.gr registry entry, updated 5 Nov 2026). AUD approximation with conversion date.

Resident vs visiting: gov.gr and Athens describe the licence for people resident in Greece; Chania and Heraklion describe foreigners living abroad bringing a marriage licence from their own country instead. Australia does not issue marriage licences, so the DFAT Certificate of No Impediment (CNI) is what Greek authorities receive (Australian Embassy Athens). Researcher must confirm how at least two popular wedding municipalities (e.g. Santorini/Thira and Mykonos) treat non-resident Australians.

Three ceremony routes in one short table: civil (legal), Greek Orthodox (legal once registered; church conditions apply), symbolic (not legal). Columns: legal status, who officiates, extra paperwork, notes for Australians.
Rules are national, but town halls apply them differently: confirm with your municipality and for your own passports (house rule).

outline.h2: Is it really an eight-day wait?
outline.answers: How long the licence actually takes, what starts the clock, what restarts it, and when it does not apply. This is the myth-busting section and must be unambiguous.
must_include: Official rule: the mayor waits one week from submission for third-party objections, then grants the licence; completion deadline 7 days (gov.gr). Athens: issued seven days after submission and verification of the documents.

What starts the clock: a complete file accepted at the counter, including the already-published newspaper notice where required. An incomplete file is returned and the process starts again (gov.gr procedure steps).
Where 'eight days' comes from: likely submit on day 0, wait seven days, collect on day 8. Present this as an explanation, not a rule, and do not name or link the commercial pages that repeat it.
If an objection is lodged, the couple is invited to respond before the licence is granted (gov.gr). One sentence; no alarmism.
When the wait does not apply: if your municipality accepts a CNI from a couple living abroad without issuing a Greek licence. Researcher to confirm per municipality.
The practical answer for planners: arrival dates should allow for weekday office hours, the week, and the registration step after the ceremony. No guarantee language.

outline.h2: The Australian documents and where each one comes from
outline.answers: Exactly which papers, which Australian office issues each, and what has to happen to each before Greece accepts it.
must_include: Table: document | issued by (state or territory BDM registry; DFAT for the CNI; Family Court for divorce) | apostille (DFAT) | Greek translation | freshness rule.

CNI: issued by DFAT through Passport Offices, missions overseas or by mail; at least one applicant must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident; ask the Greek authority whether it must be issued in Greece and whether it needs an apostille (Smartraveller CNI page, updated 1 Oct 2026). Embassy Athens: acceptable place of issue can differ significantly between organisations.

Full (long-form) birth certificates with parents' names; apostille; translation. Freshness: Athens requires documents issued within six months; other municipalities may be stricter. Researcher to source, not assume.
Previously married: divorce order or death certificate, apostilled and translated.
Current DFAT fees for CNI and apostille from the Smartraveller fees page (in AUD, dated). Do not use competitor figures.

outline.h2: Translations, Greek names and the newspaper notice
outline.answers: How the Greek-language side works when neither of you reads Greek. Addresses adapted fear: paperwork in another language.
must_include: Who may translate, sourced and current: resolve the Australian Embassy page (Greek MFA translation section or Greek consulates only) against the Ministry of Interior's 2021 circulars on the abolition of the MFA translation service and the new official translation system, and Chania's list (consulate, MFA service, Ionian University graduates, Greek lawyer). State plainly what applies in 2026 and say NAATI translations are or are not accepted only if an official source says so.
Greek consulates in Australia (Sydney covers NSW and QLD; Melbourne covers VIC and TAS, per mfa.gr) and what they can certify. Researcher to confirm current consular services.

Names: the newspaper notice and application use Greek letters, with Latin characters for a foreign spouse in Athens (Athens; Heraklion). Spelling must match across passport, birth certificate and translation.

Newspaper notice: when it is required (residents per gov.gr and Athens; some municipalities otherwise) and that the newspaper issue is submitted with the file. Do not state 'eight days before applying'.

Fees in euros paid by e-paravolo, bank or post (gov.gr). One sentence on how your concierge coordinates euro payments (brand-profile: concierge handles deposits, payments and currency across borders).

outline.h2: Civil or Greek Orthodox: how the route changes
outline.answers: What changes if one or both of you want a Greek Orthodox wedding.
must_include: Civil: officiated by the mayor or delegate; town hall or approved venue. Researcher to confirm whether non-town-hall venues are allowed and by whom.

Orthodox: the mayor's licence is required for civil marriages and for marriages solemnised by the Eastern Orthodox Church (gov.gr civil licence entry, per snippet; researcher to read in full). Church conditions (baptism, Metropolis approval, sponsor/koumbaros rules, a Christian partner) need an official church or government source or a [[NEEDS]] placeholder.
The CNI is required by religious as well as municipal bodies (Australian Embassy Athens).
Same-sex couples: civil marriage legal since Law 5089/2024 (gov.gr). Not available as an Orthodox wedding. One line plus FAQ.
Symbolic ceremony plus legal marriage in Australia as the honest alternative, with no judgement.

outline.h2: Your wedding week: town hall days, witnesses and registration
outline.answers: What actually happens on the ground and how it fits around 70 to 110 guests. This is the invisible-work section; it also answers adapted fear A (planning from the other side of the world).
must_include: Sample timetable labelled as an illustration, never a promise: e.g. documents lodged in advance by email where the municipality allows it (Chania accepts email submission), originals presented on arrival, ceremony, registration on the next working day.
Witnesses: number, age, ID; whether relatives may act (Heraklion says a witness may be a relative). Interpreter rules from an official source or [[NEEDS]].
Registration of the marriage at the registry (lixiarcheio) after the ceremony and the deadline (commonly cited as 40 days; researcher must find an official source or cut the number).

Who does what: what you must do in person versus what your concierge or a partnered planner coordinates (municipality liaison, translations, appointment timing, transfers, guest arrivals, the welcome dinner, wet-weather plan for an outdoor civil ceremony).

Official fees in one short table: licence EUR 18 (gov.gr), town-hall ceremony fees as one municipal example (Heraklion lists EUR 100 and EUR 150 by day and time; researcher to confirm currency of the 2007 decision), DFAT fees in AUD. EUR with AUD approximation and conversion date; all prices to Nic.
No guarantees about dates, approvals or turnaround.

outline.h2: Back home: is a Greek marriage valid in Australia?
outline.answers: The paying parent's question, answered with an Australian official source, plus the admin after the wedding.
must_include: Recognition of overseas marriages under Australian law (Marriage Act 1961, Part VA), sourced to the Attorney-General's Department or Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas'. No legal advice beyond the official wording.

Australia has no step to 'register' an overseas marriage; what to keep: the Greek certificate, apostille, and an English translation for Australian agencies. Researcher to confirm from official sources.
Name change: passports.gov.au evidence requirements for an overseas marriage certificate; one or two lines.
Link to our overseas marriage certificate article for the general process.
